precepts.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much. This explains why Joseph was faithful. He's in slavery now, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up. A lot of brothers and sisters have jobs; the Most High is observing us in whatever we're doing. The least that we're faithful in is these little jobs out here. Just like Joseph was in captivity, we're in captivity, but that doesn't mean we can steal, lie, or rob. When you're on your jobs, deal right. God is watching each and every one of us.
precepts.point: The Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake. You notice the theme is the same: just like when Jacob worked for Laban all those years, Laban was blessed for Jacob's sake.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Joseph was seventeen, a teenager, sold into Egypt: “Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” Yet “the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master “saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand,” and made him overseer over his house, putting all that he had into his hand.

Luke 16:10 explains why: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” Joseph was in slavery, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up.

It speaks to us today. Many brothers and sisters have jobs, and the Most High is observing us in whatever we do. The least that we are faithful in is these little jobs out here. Just as Joseph was in captivity, we are in captivity, but that does not mean we can steal, lie or rob. When you are on your jobs, do not steal; deal right. God is watching each and every one of us.

And look what faithfulness brought: “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.” The theme is the same as when Jacob worked for Laban all those years and Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake. Faithful in little, Joseph was trusted with much, until his master “knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat.”

precepts.text: That which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
precepts.point: That which is highly esteemed among men, like shellfish and bacon, is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
Everything the white man taught us is good here is bad. If you really want to go all out for your wife or your girlfriend, you buy lobster, the delicacy. The Bible says that is the scum of the earth. They have you paying $200 for a fat roach, eating clams and clam chowder, bottom feeders, rodents of the sea, and spending your hard-earned check to do it. You want to upscale a burger, put bacon on it. All of these things are abominable to God, and God is looking at us like, they have you in a trick bag. We are living in the upside-down.

Christ said it: “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” That which is highly esteemed among men is everything Esau and the nations put above God.

Justifying yourselves before men is the brothers and sisters who know the truth, who know what we are saying is right and will even say Jesus is black, but won't serve God, won't come out of the pagan holidays, and won't keep the commandments. God knows the heart.

That is how our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. We have taken what men esteem, the Sunday, the shaved face, the shellfish and the bacon, over the law of our God, and calling a bottom feeder a delicacy makes absolutely no sense. The knowledge we rejected is the laws of God.

precepts.text: Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
precepts.point: The covetous Pharisees derided him. Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.” They were mad as hell at the Messiah. Christ answered, “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts.” They are the ones going on podcasts arguing back and forth for fame, notoriety and publicity, wanting to be content creators, because “that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” In the parable that follows, the Pharisees are the rich man, and Lazarus is the disciples, us, the people under their rulership.

Those who justify themselves before men are not the ones God gathers. Christ said “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob”, and Isaiah shows who they are: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”

Thy seed: the sons and daughters of Israel scattered to the ends of the earth. God tells the north to give them up and the south not to keep them back. Those are his children, brought in from far, while the covetous Pharisees who derided Christ, children of darkness who came back as the scribes and Sadducees, are cast out. All skinfolk ain't kinfolk.

precepts.text: Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed; once judgment is passed there is no crossing it, because God is not a man that he should lie.
precepts.point: That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent.” Whatever the Lord speaks out of His mouth, once the judgment is passed there is no taking it back, whether in this life or the one to come. The parable of Lazarus shows it.

“But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

The judgment has been set and there is no changing it. A great gulf fixed, so that none can pass, because God is not a man that He should lie: hath He said, and shall He not do it?

precepts.text: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God; you could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord.
precepts.point: Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.”

What man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. You could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord. So Gideon being the least in his father's house, with no prestige to his name, was no hindrance to his calling, and it is no hindrance to yours. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

precepts.text: The sores that go unbound recall the beggar Lazarus, full of sores, in the account of Lazarus and the rich man.
precepts.point: "From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, and bruises, and putrefying sores." From the least tribe to Judah and the southern kingdom the nation is wounded, and the sores are not closed, bound up, nor mollified with ointment. The ointment that heals, whether physical or spiritual, is the word of the Most High.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

precepts.why:
“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” From the least tribe to Judah and the southern kingdom the nation is wounded. The sores that go unbound recall the beggar Lazarus: “a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores”, “desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.”

Israel is that beggar full of sores today, stricken and revolting more and more, whether earthquakes in Haiti, hurricanes in Puerto Rico and Florida, crime, or prisons filled with His chosen people. The whole head, the leadership, is sick. The sores are not closed, bound up, nor mollified with ointment, and the ointment that heals, whether physical or spiritual, is the word of the Most High.

precepts.text: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
precepts.point: If ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

precepts.why:
“But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either. Christ says it again in the parable: “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

It is the same order. Moses and the prophets come first; a man who will not hear them will not be persuaded even by one risen from the dead. They trusted in Moses, yet believed not his writings, and so they did not believe the words of the one Moses wrote of.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: We’re going to talk about the dogs for a second. “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” God is calling the Hamites dogs; the Lord is talking about the other nations.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: Remember, this is the Greek woman: “Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.” “But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” To who? To dogs. Christ is calling the Greek woman a dog: not just her, her daughter, all her people. So the reference to dogs is the other nations.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
But guess what, dogs is also talking about our people too, because our people also tend to take advantage of one another. Allegedly, in Atlanta, a brother did a whole campaign about people sending money, a Tulsa fund, like rebuilding Black Wall Street; they had a convention and raised a million dollars, and then the fund only had about seven hundred thousand dollars in it. That’s what happens.

“His watchmen are blind”: there’s a lot of watchmen, including these preachers in the hood with no education, unlearned preachers that mimic what they see the rich preachers do and open up little churches. “They are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs”: notice, he’s calling them dogs. “They cannot bark”: they can’t prophesy, they can’t teach the word of God. “Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

This year you’re going to see a bunch of dumb dogs. These pastors are going to invite Republicans and Democrats, Joe Biden, Donald Trump, senators and congressmen, inside the church to convince black people to vote for them, and when they get in office they don’t do nothing for black people. Exactly. That’s the covenant: as long as they get paid, they don’t give a damn about the people.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: “Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”: they always want give me, give me, give me. “And they are shepherds that cannot understand”: shepherds that cannot understand the word of God. That’s what we read in 2 Esdras 9: they have not known me. “They all look to their own way, every one for his gain”, his financial gain, “from his quarter”: his church.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: start at verse 5. “Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.”

“And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee”: thy seed after thee is talking about Israel, “in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.” That covenant that was made with Abraham, that’s his bosom. We going to inherit all the blessings that were given to Abraham.

“And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land wherein thou art a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.” That’s going to be the area of New Jerusalem; in fact Jerusalem is going to be larger than that.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things: go right back to 2 Esdras 9. “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments. For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”. It’s not saying anything different; it’s saying the same thing. The good things the rich man received in his lifetime are the benefits.

“And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; The same must know it after death by pain.” By what? By pain. So Christ is saying, now it’s your turn to be tormented.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord”: this is talking about the kingdom, so we know the kingdom is set up at this time.

Here it come: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”: you broke the commandments, you rejected Christ. “For their worm shall not die”: their worm is their soul; their soul shall not die. “Neither shall their fire be quenched.”

So that’s in the kingdom, and like Abraham and Lazarus seeing the rich man across the gulf, they go forth and look upon them. When the kingdom is established, that’s why Christ said he has the keys to death and hell; when he returns, this is what he’s going to do.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: They have Moses and the prophets: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?”

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: He said if one went unto them from the dead they will repent. “Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” Christ had just raised Lazarus from the dead. “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”. You see how wicked these are? These are wicked as hell. One came back from the dead, and instead of repenting they wanted to kill him again.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” That’s right.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Remember, Christ had just resurrected. “Behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done”: the stone was moved away and Christ was gone, the body was gone. “And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers, Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.”

They concocted a lie. When you read it, the angel came down, the guards got frightened and fled, the stone was moved away and Christ came out. But the elders said no, here’s some money, you’re going to say this lie. “And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.” That also puts more of a bounty on the apostles’ heads: you broke Pilate’s seal and went in there and stole a body, so we got to arrest these guys.

“So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.” One rose from the dead, and they were not persuaded.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Full of sores: “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores”. Look up in the chapter who it’s talking about. It is Israel, so when we go back to Luke 16:20, we know that Lazarus, full of sores, represents our people.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Verse 4 tells you who Isaiah 1:6 is talking about: “Ah sinful nation”. Verse 3: “The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” The one with the putrifying sores is Israel, our people, and that is the beggar Lazarus full of sores.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
The rich man’s table is the scribes and Pharisees, and it goes perfectly with James 5: those rich men that held back the labourers’ pay by fraud. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

Who gave them their place and nation? The Romans gave them theirs. Just like all of these politicians and these pastors: America gave them those seats of authority. America’s the one that chooses black leaders who’s going to do what we say. They got those positions from America. So it’s the same thing back during the time of Christ.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: “Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” Now these dogs: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” So the dogs in Exodus is making reference to the Egyptians.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: “Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me. But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” It is not right to take the children’s bread, to take my healing power, and to cast it to dogs. So Christ called this woman of another nation a dog. So far we have the Egyptians in Exodus 11 and this woman here in Matthew 15.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Who’s this woman? The verse tells you her race: “behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David”. She is of another nation, and that is the woman Christ calls a dog.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
“His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs”. That includes our people too: God is calling them dumb dogs, ’cause the white man set some of our people up as watchmen along with other nations. “They cannot bark”: they cannot warn the people of danger, “sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber. Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”.

Like what we showed today with the brother Billy Carson: you would be considered a dog, because you’re reaping financial gain from a poor and destitute people and you’re not helping us at all; you’re just giving us lies after lies after lies. So the dogs that licked Lazarus’s sores are the other nations and the wicked of our people as well.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Mark tells the same account as Matthew 15: “The woman was a Greek”. “But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.” So you got the Egyptians in Exodus 11, you got the woman from Canaan in Matthew 15, a Greek in Mark 7: the dogs are the other nations.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
Now don’t get mad, get glad. “And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” The whole planet is going to be forced to observe the new moon holiday and the Sabbath; everybody’s going to be made to obey.

“And they shall go forth”: that’s the righteous shall go forth, “and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die”: their worm, that’s about their soul; it shall not die. “Neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” You see those people over there screaming, those rebellious ones against the Lord? Everybody is going to see them spirits.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
Y’all keep playing. You got camps telling you you can eat pork and it’s good in Yahawashi; that ain’t gonna work, and bragging about it. You got camps saying you could buy prostitutes and it’s good in Yahawashi. Y’all keep being fooled by these people out here.

“And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched”. Now you telling me nothing’s going to happen when you die? You a liar, brother; I’m reading it.

What does it mean, cut your hand off? Deuteronomy 13 shows it. So the hand offending you is a friend, a mother, a son, a daughter, somebody close to you, somebody important to you. Cut it off: it’s better to enter the kingdom without that person than to have that person with you and go into hell, where the fire shall never be quenched. “Where their worm dieth not”: where your soul does not die, “and the fire is not quenched.”

“And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off”: this is still mother, father, son, daughter or friend. Better to enter in without that person “than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched”. Christ is still repeating it, so should we listen to Christ or listen to the frenemies online? “And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out”: again that eye represents your mother, father, your wife, your son or daughter. “It is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.”

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
What it means to cut off the hand that offends you: “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers; Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth”. What we going to do? “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him: But thou shalt surely kill him”. That was under Moses: “thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death”.

Look at verse 6 again: or your precious little daughter; or the wife of your bosom, you brother, you just so in love; or some of you got a friend you cannot do without, “which is as thine own soul”, that friend grew up with you all your life. “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him”. With that thought, the hand in Mark 9 is that person close to you.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why:
Y’all keep playing with these dumb Israelites out there; stop listening to them. You got women talking about, I’m mad with my husband, I’m getting me a new man. Women get passed around in these places like Skittles, and they think there’s no judgment for that.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways”: which now have abused God’s way, his laws. You got the Bible but you’re doing wrong with the understanding; you manipulate the people. “And they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments”: you’re going to live in torments. Keep playing.

“For such as in their life have received benefits”, like the rich man we reading about, “and have not known me; And they that have loathed my law”, they that hated God’s law, “while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it”: they despised repentance. Here’s the point: “The same must know it after death by pain.” The dude on the YouTube talking about it don’t mean what it mean: you going to learn. You going to suffer by pain; you going to learn then.

That is the rich man in hell, in torments, and that is what Abraham tells him: he received his good things in his lifetime, he had benefits in this world.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: The great gulf fixed. “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” That’s Old Testament; now we’re in the New Testament saying the same thing. There’s no contradiction: they shall look upon them, and between us and them is a gulf no one can pass.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Though one rose from the dead, they would not be persuaded. When Christ raised Lazarus, what was the plot? “Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”: they would put him to death. That’s how wicked these Israelites were. “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” These dudes were so wicked: a man was raised from the dead and they plotted to kill that man. We got to put that dude back to death? The hell is this.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

precepts.why: Remember what Abraham told the rich man: they got Moses and the prophets, and if they won’t hear them, they won’t hear one risen from the dead. Christ says the same: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.” That’s just for all you Christians out there: Moses wrote of Christ. “But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” And that goes for some of you Israelites that say, I don’t believe in no JC. There’s no magic scripture; some of y’all we cannot help.

note.label: Job The Black Prophet And Our People Today

precepts.why:
About our people. “And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: the 12 tribes of Israel died, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: that’s the elect of the 12 tribes.

“The rich man also died, and was buried”: our people who sided with Rome, who side with America, also died. “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments”: in hell, destruction, he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, “and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.” That is the rich man of Job who opens his eyes and is not.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why:
Christ said unto the Pharisees, “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.”

Bring that up to today: many of our people esteem Hollywood stars and entertainers, and Christ said that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination. Anybody that is esteemed in this society, Christ is letting us know, has committed abomination; there are things they have done behind the scenes to get where they are. So whether the gossip about some big preacher is true or not, we don’t know and don’t give a dag on; it has nothing to do with us. We stick with what the Bible says, not with being a busybody in other men’s matters.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Here is the precept for understanding why: “And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falleth, he shall find a stay.” When you fall you shall find help.

So if you deal right with people on your job, when you need help they will help you. But if you’re on your job acting like a nuka, nobody is gonna help you when you need it.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
This is for you brothers who put your job ahead of God’s work. “They shall not be sought for in publick counsel, nor sit high in the congregation”: don’t look for rank if your job is your first priority.

“They shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment”: don’t ask why you don’t understand certain judgments. You’ve not been around, you’ve not studied, you’ve not prayed nor applied, but you’ve gone to work sun up to sundown every day. “They cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken”: when we’re going over parables you’re nowhere around.

“But they will maintain the state of the world”: your whole life is maintaining the United States of America. “And all their desire is in the work of their craft.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: We’re going to talk about the rich man. “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” This letter is addressed to the twelve tribes.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Still addressed to the twelve tribes. “Go to now, ye rich men”: it’s addressing the rich men of the twelve tribes of Israel. This goes with some of your athletes, your actors, your entertainers.

“Weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you”: when he says weep and howl for your misery, he’s saying you better repent. “Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten. Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you”.

Sometimes we read about the rich man and don’t realize Israelites were rich. The rich man of Luke 16 is a rich man of Israel.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
A certain beggar: who is this beggar? “He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory”. Dunghill means doo-doo; y’all know, s-h-i-t.

That precept right there goes with the beggar in Luke 16:20. The beggar is the poor of Israel that the Lord raises up out of the dust to inherit the throne of glory.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: The dogs are other nations, and here’s the proof. About Egypt: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” So God is calling the Egyptians dogs.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “Moab is my washpot”: that’s why they’re always in the laundromats. “Over Edom will I cast out my shoe”: you know how you throw your shoe at a dog. Down South we love to throw our shoes at a dog, because they ain’t right, trying to sneak in the house and eat somebody’s food. “Over Philistia will I triumph”: Philistia is Palestine, the Palestinians.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Remember the dogs licked the sores of Lazarus: that’s the nations taking our wealth and our riches. Everything we’re about to read, the majority of it, 99.9, they get from the continent of Africa.

“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: The merchandise of gold”: they get that from Africa. “and precious stones”, from Africa, “and of pearls”, from Africa, “and fine linen”, “and purple”, from Africa, “and silk”, from Africa and Madagascar, “and scarlet”, “and all manner vessels of ivory”, “and of brass, and iron, and marble”, “And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat”, “and sheep, and horses”, “and slaves, and souls of men”: all from Africa.

These are the things they do to our people, the Shemites who live on the continent. These are the dogs that lick the sores: they take, they take, they take from us. When we’ve been through Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone, this is what you’ll see: sit down in a restaurant to eat, you’ll always see an Edomite with our people. They have deceived our people into thinking they’re going to benefit from a business. They just put the blacks as the face over the company, but behind the scenes it’s always the white man reaping all the financial benefits. They’ll give the blacks maybe a dollar more here and a dollar there, and our people really think they have made it. Some of our people will curse you, spit at you, look down on you, because they are working with the white man. We saw it in Sierra Leone and Nigeria, the same thing: I am with the white man, my brother, he is God, you are nothing.

They hire Africans, and a lot of them are our people, and pay them pennies on the dollar to do the mining and things of that nature. The map of Africa: mine, mine, mine, for the diamonds in South Africa, the gold in Ghana. This is what Esau and the nations do, because it ain’t just Esau: it’s China doing it, the Arabs doing it too. And Esau behind the scenes is filthy rich. They are the dogs.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
How do you know the white man’s a dog? Here’s another scripture proof that they’re the dogs Christ was talking about. “And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid”: Christ couldn’t be hid, he was so famous. “For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation”: she was a Greek, meaning she was Syrian and lived in Phenicia. “And she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.”

“But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.” Cast it unto who? The dogs. The churches never explained it: he’s insulting her. There’s an s: he didn’t say dog, he said dogs, for her and her people, her daughter, her people. Dogs is plural. Nobody in Christianity wants to stay on that; they want to run by it. No, let’s pause right there and talk about this. This loving Jesus called her dogs, not just her, but her daughter’s a dog and her people are dogs. That’s your mama a dog; that’s what the Son of God is saying right there. That’s what you got to do on the street: don’t let them run by that.

“And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.” What did she do? Yes, Lord. She admitted she’s a dog. Y’all try to get the white man to admit that. “And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.” That’s what you got to stress: for this saying. What saying? That she was a dog and her people are dogs. No Christian wants to deal with that. They want you to keep reading and just run; read on, read quick. No, we’re going to read this slow. The other nations are dogs.

Some brothers use that and say a dog is a female, b-i-t-c-h. You brothers know: we got to use the words in the Bible. She’s a dog, her child is a dog, her people, all the men in her nation, are dogs. They’ll understand. Don’t try to be slick and do your own thing talking about a dog is a b-i-t-c-h, so Christ called her a b-i-t-c-h. No.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Not only are the other nations dogs, but rich and wicked Israelites are dogs. “His watchmen are blind”: the white man has set up watchmen, and the watchmen he set up are our people, as taskmasters. They can’t understand, they can’t see the scriptures.

“They are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark”: a dog barking is meant to warn you. These dumb dogs, these Pharisees, cannot warn the people of impending doom. “Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”: always want money, money, money. “And they are shepherds that cannot understand”: shepherds that can’t understand the word of God. “They all look to their own way, every one for his gain”: for his own gain, money, money, money, “from his quarter”: from wherever his church is set up, that’s what it means, from his quarter.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept of his watchmen. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

So who set the scribes and Pharisees up in their positions? The Romans. These Pharisees and Sadducees, these religious leaders, were the watchmen, the dumb dogs of Isaiah 56:10.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
We see that Christ called them dogs; here’s another one. “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me”. When Christ was on the cross it wasn’t just the Romans that were around him. You had the scribes and Pharisees saying, he calls on Elijah, let’s see if he’s going to be saved: they were making mockery of the Son of God while he was on the cross.

“They pierced my hands and my feet”: that was the Romans. “I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog.” The dog that had power at that time was with the Romans. You had these wicked scribes and Pharisees doing the will of Rome, so they all fall in that dog category.

What has that got to do with us today? Today our people do the bidding of the Christian church: the Vatican, the Protestant Christians. They are dogs. Your famous, world-renowned Christian pastors are dogs: their bishops, the deacons, the ushers, the deaconesses, all dogs. Give me ten of your earnings: all of them are dogs.

And don’t forget the wicked Israelites today, the ones with the mouth speaking evil against their brothers. They’re dogs too, because eventually they’re going to join with Esau to come against us. I’m talking to you: you are a dog.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
More precepts on dogs. “There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” Now watch what Moses calls the whore and the sodomite. “Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore, or the price of a dog, into the house of the Lord thy God for any vow: for even both these are abomination unto the Lord thy God.”

Don’t bring the hire of a whore: you make money off a whore, the Lord said I don’t want that money. Neither the price of a dog: that sodomite, you made money off that, don’t bring that money into the temple. It’s calling our people in them lifestyles dogs.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
We’re still talking about dogs, and remember, these dogs feed off of our people, the poor of our people. “For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ”: that’s you men and women listening now that claim you’ve repented. “They are again entangled therein”: you get entangled in your former sins, “and overcome”: you get overcome by your former sins. “The latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them”: you left the commandments of God.

“But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb”: watch what it calls you. “The dog is turned to his own vomit again”: you’re a dog that has returned to your own vomit again. “And the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire”: you’re a pig.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” The only way you get into the gates of the city, we got to keep the commandments.

“For without are dogs”: outside New Jerusalem are dogs, that’s the other nations, “and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie.” So you ain’t getting in.

We’ve read all these precepts to help us understand the parable of Lazarus. Now that we went through them, it helps us understand what Christ is talking about with the dogs that licked his sores.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: Here’s the evidence that they won’t be persuaded though one rose from the dead. “Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” Remember in history, Christ raised Lazarus from the dead.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”. Do y’all see that? They wanted to put Lazarus to death, “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

Then the people “took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord”, and Jesus sat on a young ass, as it is written, “Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.” “The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.”

When Lazarus was raised from the dead, those same wicked scribes and Pharisees plotted and planned to put Lazarus to death. That’s why Abraham said to the rich man, if they don’t believe Moses and the prophets, they won’t believe though one rose from the dead.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

points: The covetous Pharisees derided him. Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

points: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men. That is what they do. Tell them Christmas is a pagan holiday: no, that is just a day me and my family get together. Thanksgiving is a celebration of the slaughter and murder of your people: no, that's just a day me and family get together. But you still have a Christmas tree, you decorate it and you still give gifts. You still do the custom, but you try to justify it in your mind. You are of the world.

But as soon as you say we keep Passover, the Feast of Dedication, the Sabbath day, the new moon, the feast days: oh no, you ain't supposed to be doing all of that. I could celebrate pagan holidays, but if I celebrate God's holidays that are written in the Bible, I'm wrong. Y'all make no sense, and the people are going to wake up and realize that.

That which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God. What is highly esteemed among men? Christmas, Thanksgiving, New Year's, birthdays; the way our women dress out of order; prostituting your daughters.

Yes, you are prostituting your daughters: giving them boyfriends, giving your daughter over to a man that is not her husband, allowing a young man with no plan in life to deal with your daughter, knowing that boys only want one thing.

Y'all let them go to prom, pay for the out of order dresses, slits all the way up to the hip, dressed tight as hell, let these young boys pick them up, pay for the limo, and some of y'all even give them hotel rooms. Don't pimps do the same thing? Buy the women their clothes, their food, and when the johns come, buy the hotel room. That is prostitution, and you allow your daughters to do that because it is highly esteemed among men. Shame on y'all.

note.label: When the World Loves It's Own

points: The righteous are always going to have to deal with the ungodly. But you can make your life harder by cutting off relationships with the ungodly, or being rude to them, or tell them that they're going to die. No. The scripture say walk in wisdom toward them that are without.

Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness: so does God say sever relationships, meaning cut them off? No. The Lord is saying don't sin for them. Don't break God laws for him. Don't trim your ways. Do like I do. I make jokes with them. I have a good time with them. But I don't sin for him. When it's Christmas, I'm not going over there. New Year's, I'm not going. I'm not calling you up on your birthday. No. Because it's against the laws of God.

That, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations: if you fall, you might need their help one day, or they might repent. You just never know. But if you treating the ungodly rude and evil, nobody's going to want to deal with you.

Now look, a lot of us come in truth and have underage children. Now that's really tough when you have underage children like teenagers, 14, 15, 16, that grew up in Babylon the Great learning all of the fake holidays, and that stuff is fun, right? Christmas is fun. New Year's is fun. Fourth of July is fun. A lot of them don't want to let that go because that's all they know. That's when the book becomes bitter. But guess what? We have to be subject to the laws. We can't just put our underage children out.

note.label: Ungodly Children

points: A parable that Christ gave us. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. The rich man who fared sumptuously is those ministers, those politicians, those Israelites who have received benefits: they got money, fame and fortune, and everybody loves them. This rich man does not represent Rome, and it does not represent the white man.

Remember what we read earlier: the rulers of our people have made a covenant with death and hell. They made an agreement with Rome, just like today these ministers have made an agreement with the United States of America: keep these people in sin, keep these people in lies, and as long as we get paid we good.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores”. Lazarus represents the Israelites, the repentant Israelites.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: our people want the crumbs that the leaders of our society have. That’s the welfare and all that, the low paying jobs. When they in Congress fighting for jobs, the jobs we getting are not jobs to be CEOs; we get jobs to be workers. The ministers say I’m going to go to Congress and fight for you, and you get a job, you get a job.

“Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” The dogs are the nations, and also these low-level preachers. The nations open up businesses, like the Chinese and the Italians, in poor communities, and take, take, take so that they can build their communities, but meanwhile we stay impoverished.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: I gave you more than one death, and that’s death right there. He “was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: Abraham’s bosom is the covenant made with Abraham, the blessings we are going to inherit.

“The rich man also died”: the one that was in purple and fared sumptuously every day, he died, “and was buried”. This rich man represents all people that have benefits in this world. They die, and now they in the grave.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments”. That hell is the torment. It’s the same torment we read in 2 Esdras 9, and it’s the same thing Christ said in Matthew 23:33 about damnation. He “seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.”

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.” Tormented in what? In this flame. This is what Christ said: fear him that can destroy both body and soul in hell.
It ain’t talking about, like the church say, the middle of the earth. It’s still another realm, another dimension; that’s what it’s going into.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”: what was the word we read in 2 Esdras 9? Benefits. “And likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted”, comforted in the bosom of Abraham, the kingdom, because that’s what it’s talking about, “and thou art tormented.” Now it’s your turn to be tormented. You thought you got away with that good life, but now you’re tormented.
I know what you’re thinking: I thought you read in Job we all at peace. Remember, Christ said he has the keys of hell and death.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.” That’s how you know it’s another realm, another dimension. This great gulf is another dimension, another realm. They couldn’t go to them and they can’t come to us, but they could see: Abraham and Lazarus could see the rich man in torment, but they could not reach one another.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren”. Look at the five brothers: they living good, they living lavish, they got women, they got fortune, they got wealth, they got it all. “That he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” That’s how you know this rich man ain’t Esau. It says they have Moses and the prophets: that’s about Israel. The Israelites got Moses and the prophets. Let them hear them: let them study their scriptures.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.” That’s a lie. They never would repent.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” They won’t be persuaded if one rose from the dead, and Matthew 28 shows it.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: I went over this before, but I want to touch it again. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. In this parable it goes into some real stuff. The rich man is the rich man of Israel, like we read in James 5 and Matthew 19.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus”. Lazarus represents the elect of our people, the poor. Remember what we read earlier in 1 Samuel 2: he will lift up the beggar from the dunghill. So Lazarus here is this beggar, “laid at his gate, full of sores”. And with Isaiah 1 we know that Lazarus here represents our people.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: he wanted crumbs, he wanted a little handout. The rich man’s table is the chief priests and the Pharisees, and it goes perfectly with James 5: those rich men that held back your payment of labour by fraud. That’s what these people was doing.

“Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” The dogs are the other nations, and the wicked of our people as well. When it says the dogs licked his sores, they took advantage, like these other nations move into our communities and set up stores and all that.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: he dropped dead, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: carried by the angels into the promise of Abraham. Abraham’s bosom, that’s going into the kingdom. “The rich man also died, and was buried”.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.” This is crazy, because you get people, frenemies, that say when you die you die, that’s it. Now we know you die today, you at rest; we know that. But when Christ comes and opens that realm, ’cause them missiles going to hit, it’s going to be a lake of fire; yes, all that’s true. There will be a realm in there where you will not escape. You have done wickedness all your lives and you going to escape? Okay, that makes a lot of sense.
He saw Abraham far off in the distance, and Lazarus was enjoying the kingdom.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.”

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”: that’s what we just read in Esdras. You had benefits in this world. “And likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted”: Lazarus is comforted in the kingdom, “and thou art tormented”: you’re being tormented.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed”: that’s what we read in Isaiah 66. “So that they which would pass from hence to you cannot”: that’s how you know it’s another realm. We will not be allowed to pass to them, “neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren”: five brothers, all womanizers, filthy rich, “that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” This lets you know these are Israelites. They got Moses and the prophets. Esau did not have Moses and the prophets; Jacob had Moses and the prophets. So it’s talking about Israelites. And they had Moses and the prophets right there in their day, and they were still not going to listen to them.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: “If one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.” “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” So there is no magic scripture. When Christ rose from the dead they still didn’t believe, and when he raised Lazarus, they plotted to kill Lazarus.

note.label: Pride & Divine Judgment

points: This goes with cutting off the family members or friends that cause you to sin. “Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness”: it seems like a contradiction, Christ telling us to make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness. Mammon is wealth regarded as an evil influence or false object of worship; in the Bible it is the term for riches, often used for the debasing influence of material wealth. The mammon of unrighteousness is the people in the world that don’t believe the truth.

Verses 1 through 8 are the parable of an unjust steward that dealt unwisely and got fired from his job, and he had to deal right with people so they would help him. So Christ says make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness, “that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: Don’t get trapped serving this world for money. “No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. Serving mammon means you got that covetous spirit: everything you do is about money. You can’t serve two gods; when you’re serving mammon, meaning riches, that’s your god. “Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” You got to love one and hate the other. Make your choice.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: I wanted to preach up this parable with those scriptures. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. Let’s see who this rich man is. You know some of your preachers look like that.

Sometimes we read about the rich man and we don’t realize Israelites were rich. Some of them, not all of them. Nicodemus was rich; Joseph of Arimathea was rich; remember the young man that was rich, and Christ said sell all that you got and give to the poor, and he went away sorrowful; Zacchaeus, who was a tax collector, was rich; Paul was rich at one time. These rich men are the type of rich people amongst us that you see today.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores”. Who is this beggar? The beggar is the one the Lord lifts up from the dunghill to set among princes.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: that’s the little benefits we get in society. “Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” Who are these dogs? Write this down: the dogs cover two things. The dogs are both other nations and wicked Israelites, and it is proven from the scriptures.

A lot of our people live in America, we’re scattered worldwide, and a large proportion of us live on the continent of Africa. The dogs licking the sores of Lazarus is the nations taking our wealth and our riches.

Think about it: you have a black community, a black and Latino community. These nations always set up shop where we live, get all the money they can get from us, and then take it back to their people. We don’t reap the benefits of nothing. This is what the story of Lazarus is about.
And remember, these dogs feed off of our people, the poor of our people. That’s what they do.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: Lazarus dies, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”. Abraham’s bosom is paradise. “The rich man also died, and was buried”.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And in hell”: at the beginning of the lesson it talked about hell being everlasting fire, remember that. “He lift up his eyes, being in torments”. Being in what? Torment. Now remember, that torment comes when Christ returns.

All this is spiritual. We know once the bombs hit, brothers and sisters, your flesh is gone instantly, but your spirit stays around. “And seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom”: Lazarus is with him.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.” See that: I am tormented in this flame. This flame, we know, is the spiritual side of it, because the physical, your flesh, is gone already. But your spirit, the real you, that’s what we read in Daniel 12: everlasting shame and contempt.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”. Remember in the book of Esdras the Bible said they received benefits: ‘such as in their life have received benefits’. “And likewise Lazarus evil things”: evil things, poverty, oppression. “But now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.” Lazarus, which represents the repentant, is comforted, but now is your turn to be tormented. That’s the same shall know it after death by pain.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot”: there’s nobody that can get over there to you. This is the spiritual realm. In the spiritual realm it’s not permitted for us to even go to you; we can’t get there even if we wanted to. “Neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence”: neither can you come from there to us. This is all in the spirit realm.

Abraham will literally see them being tormented, but the gulf is fixed: they are in the spirit realm being tormented while Abraham is in the kingdom of God with Christ, and there’s nothing that can be done. We can’t go to the spirit world and bring you alive.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house”: send Lazarus to my father’s house, “For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets”. This is how you know the rich man is Israel: they have who? Moses. “Let them hear them”: let them hear what Moses and the prophets said; that way they could avoid this place.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, they won’t even believe if somebody rises from the dead.
Some of y’all, even in here, think if your parents see some wonder they’re going to believe. No: if they were wicked in the past, they’re going to be wicked today.
